title: Notable recent AI papers on arXiv — weekly — 2026-11-07 to 2026-11-13
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; the ordering is inferred from checkable evidence, not popularity, and citation evidence is limited for papers only days old.

sections.title: Towards Reliable VLM Judges: State-Conditional Invariance and Presentation-Aware Diagnostics
sections.abstract: The paper proposes a simulator-grounded diagnostic benchmark for testing whether vision-language judges remain stable under semantics-preserving presentation changes while changing verdicts when counterfactual task outcomes change.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce State-Conditional Invariance and GridWM-Judge, which pairs full, evidence-removed, and counterfactual trajectories to diagnose presentation stability and causal sensitivity.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors characterize the benchmark as a controlled diagnostic, not a deployment-readiness test; its core MiniGrid tasks omit real-world sensor noise, continuous control, and open-ended robot behavior.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv record reports acceptance to NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations and Datasets); the paper also links a project, code, and dataset, and is cross-listed in four core AI categories.

sections.title: Early Signals, Strong Decisions: Prefix-Guided Sampling for Parallel Test-Time Scaling
sections.abstract: Prefix-Guided Sampling (PreG) ranks short reasoning prefixes with internal confidence signals and spends further generation only on promising candidates, aiming to improve parallel test-time reasoning with fewer tokens.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine prefix-level confidence ranking with selective continuation and report improved results over the tested parallel-sampling baselines, with lower token use in most of 60 reported configurations.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that gains depend on confidence-signal quality and that PreG may not beat the baseline at very small token budgets; the reported results cover particular models, benchmarks, and settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper is listed in the NeurIPS 2026 program and releases code and a dataset; its placement reflects a checkable conference/program signal and reproducible artifacts, rather than citation momentum.

sections.title: Emergent Vision-Shaped Thinking in Text-Only Reasoning through Multimodal Training
sections.abstract: Through causal ablations across multimodal configurations, the authors report that vision-language training can shape hidden representations used for some text-only spatial reasoning tasks, while leaving tested symbolic tasks relatively unaffected.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors identify and intervene on vision-language directions in hidden-state space, reporting a 27.6 percentage-point drop on one spatial navigation task after ablation while a tested Boolean task did not show the same decline.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors limit the conclusions to accessible model families and mostly linear or low-rank interventions; their diagnostic task battery is not a complete account of reasoning, and some effects vary by architecture and capability.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work appears in the NeurIPS 2026 program and spans the AI and computer-vision categories; the full paper reports controlled ablations across 10 configurations from six model families.

sections.title: Specify Privacy Yourself: Assessing Inference-Time Personalized Privacy Preservation Ability of Large Vision-Language Models
sections.abstract: The paper introduces SPY-Bench for testing whether vision-language models can apply user-specified, context-dependent privacy boundaries to image-question pairs, and reports low compliance for most tested models alongside an initial alignment method.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors construct a 32,700-sample benchmark spanning 67 categories and 24 scenarios, evaluate 21 LVLMs, and report that their initial noise-contrastive alignment method reaches 96.88% accuracy on their evaluation.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors present the alignment result as an initial step; benchmark performance on the specified categories and scenarios does not establish protection for arbitrary users, contexts, or image data.
sections.announcement_type: new submission; arXiv posting of work accepted at ACM Multimedia 2025
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv record identifies this work as accepted to ACM Multimedia 2025 (Brave New Ideas track), and its five-category cross-list gives it unusually broad AI relevance in this weekly pool. The arXiv posting is new this week; the underlying conference work is not new research from 2026.

sections.title: Embodied First Exam
sections.abstract: The authors introduce an agent-native benchmark with 1,156 tasks across 35 suites and 47 robots, allowing coding agents to choose direct control, code-based control, or policy training and measuring failures under several simulator settings.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide an evaluation framework that lets coding agents select their control strategy and labels the stage where attempts fail; the abstract reports 34% success for the strongest of eight agents on 456 core tasks in the Standard Setting.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a benchmark result, not evidence of equivalent success on physical robots; the reported 34% is specific to one agent and the benchmark's core-task Standard Setting.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The benchmark has a public project site and repository, and the paper is cross-listed in robotics and AI; its breadth and runnable artifacts support inclusion as a notable benchmark contribution.

sections.title: LEGION: Benchmarking Language Agents on Sparse-Signal Investigation Under Adversarial Noise
sections.abstract: LEGION combines a stochastic enterprise-telemetry simulator, 74 adversarial scenarios, and an evaluation protocol for investigation efficiency and detection accuracy; in the reported tests, five agent architectures achieve high recall but lower precision.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a sparse-signal, adversarial investigation benchmark and report recall of 0.82–0.88 versus precision of 0.61–0.72 across five agents on two simulated companies.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evidence is limited to five architectures and two simulated companies, so performance and failure patterns need validation on broader or operational telemetry.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors release the simulator, scenario library, and evaluation pipeline; a separate benchmark digest also surfaced the work. Inclusion is based on its concrete, reproducible agent-evaluation contribution, not demonstrated citation growth.

content.theme: Evaluation is becoming more diagnostic than a single score
content.summary: GridWM-Judge separates presentation stability from causal sensitivity; Embodied First Exam labels failure stages; LEGION scores investigation efficiency alongside detection. These are related approaches, not one shared standard.

content.theme: Selective inference-time compute and mechanistic testing
content.summary: PreG selects promising prefixes for continuation, while the EVT study uses causal interventions to test representations used in text-only spatial reasoning. These are method-level signals in this selected set.

Specify Privacy Yourself evaluates user-defined boundaries, while GridWM-Judge tests whether decisions change for causal rather than presentation reasons; these are isolated examples in the shortlist.
GridWM-Judge is controlled and omits real sensor noise and continuous control; Embodied First Exam reports benchmark rather than physical-robot results; LEGION tests two simulated companies.
Evaluate held-out tasks in noisy simulators and physical or operational settings, retaining causal labels and reporting accuracy plus control/investigation cost.
PreG depends on confidence-signal quality and may not beat baselines at very small budgets.
Run budget sweeps across model families and tasks, calibrate prefix scores against eventual correctness, and identify when selection should defer to full sampling.
EVT is bounded by accessible models, diagnostic tasks, and mostly linear or low-rank interventions.
Test nonlinear and cross-attention interventions on held-out model families with task-matched controls for spatial reasoning versus general state tracking.
SPY-Bench and its initial alignment method cover specified categories and scenarios, not all user-defined privacy rules.
Evaluate unseen users and contexts, measure privacy leakage alongside task utility, and test policy persistence across multi-turn interactions and image types.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The clearest signal in this selected set is a push to measure how systems fail, not just whether they produce the right final answer. Transfer from controlled diagnostics to less curated tasks and real operating conditions remains to be tested.
